exposure: Active management of the birthing process (interventionist approach)
outcome: Geographic variations in shoulder dystocia rates
Chronologic fluctuations in shoulder dystocia rates
cohort: The study analyzed reported statistics on shoulder dystocia from the USA and 11 other countries, and evaluated 104 well-documented cases of shoulder arrest at birth that resulted in permanent neonatal damage.
finding: The incidence of shoulder dystocia has increased about fourfold in the USA since the mid-twentieth century, with more than two-thirds of injured fetuses being extracted from the birth canal within 2 minutes after shoulder arrest.
mod_finding: The escalation of shoulder dystocia incidents in the USA since the 1980s is attributed largely to the introduction of 'active management' (interventionist approach) of the birthing process, replacing a conservative philosophy.
cross-section timing: Trends analyzed from the middle of the twentieth century, and cases evaluated over the last four decades.
